W72137 F.C. MOST UNIQUE TELEPHONE EXCHANGE IN THE WORLD.
"China" exchange of San Francisco is no doubt the most unique of it's kind in the world. The building is considered one of the most beautiful specimens of Chinese architecture, the equal of which is seldom seen outside of the Celestial Empire. The pagodas or towers are receding stories with gaily colored roofs tunnel up sharply and highly ornamental. The shape is supposed to shelter the building from the direct rays of the suns and also to throw the rain water free from the building. In China the roof is the principle ornament of the billing, it being considered a sign of dignity to possess several roofs, one over the other. The interior is elaborately furnish in true Occidental style, dragons and Chinese designs in-colors prevailing. The interior woodwork is finished in black ebony and gold and an attractive Torri or Shrime at the end of the room forms an appropriate setting for the handsomely carved switchboard and its native operators. She has specialized in this study for four years, Miss Phang, who was born in the Island of Jamaica of Chinese parents, plans and business and political career for herself in China. CHINESE WEDDING
Costly Silks from China

Most of the well-known Chinese residents of Sydney and many Australian friends assembled at St. Andrew's Cathedral yesterday afternoon for the wedding of Mr. James Peter Chong, son of Mrs. Chong, of Ashfield, with Miss Lucy Edna Goon.

The wedding group was unusually pretty, many of the handsome materials used in the dresses being brought from Hongkong by the bridegroom's sisters. The pretty olive-skinned bride, who was given away by her brother, Mr. Fred Goon, was charmingly gowned in white Chinese satin, trimmed with silver lace and Chinese brocade. The train was of white satin, lined with pink nimon and ornamented with silver true lovers' knots and orange blossoms. An embroidered net veil was held in place with an orange bud wreath. The bridal bouquet was of graceful, trailing silk roses and natural asparagus fern.

A bevy of bridesmaids, flower girls and train-bearers attended the bride, and included five sisters of the bridegroom. Miss Minnie Chong and her sister, Sarah, wore white hand-embroidered frocks, made in China, and hats of deep rose and silver brocade. Tulle sashes in the same shade of rose finished the waists. Misses Pearl and Ivy Chong, twin sisters, wore pale Nile green Chinese brocade, flounced with white Chandilly lace, and white hats. The little flower girls, Miss Sylvia Chong, Miss Thelma Yin, and Miss Phyllis Quay,{nieces of the bridegroom, wore the faintest shade in pink net frocks over white, with big pink net chooux in their hair. The effect of the little girls in their frilly frocks with the great baskets of pink and white flowers, veiled in tulle, was exceedingly dainty.

Dr. James Kem Yee, of Sydney Hospital, was best man, and Mr. William Yan was groomsman. The ceremony was performed by the Rev. Canon Charlton, and Mr. V. Massey presided at the organ. During the signing of the register, Miss Sadie Lewis sang. Because, Following the Chinese custom, the bridegroom's mother afterwards entertained about 200 friends at Sargent's Burlington cafe.

W72136 F.C. MOST UNIQUE TELEPHONE EXCHANGE IN THE WORLD. The most unique telephone exchange in the world exists in San Francisco's Chinatown. Here we have the ancient tongues and customs of the Orient linked with the most modern and intellectual of the Occident. The home of the exchange is considered one of the most beautiful specimens of Chinese architecture, the equal of which is seldom seen outside the Celestial empire. In this building as well as all chinese buildings, the roof is the principal ornament of thebuilding. The ceiling of the main operating room, which is photographed here with Oriental beauties at the switchboard is freseeded with dragons and Chinese designs, which would seem to run riot with each other, but which are strictly in conformity with Chinese conception of art. The interior woodwork is finished in black ebony and gold and an attractive Torri or Shrime at the end of the room forms an appropriate setting for the handsomely carved switchboard and its native operators. The operators, of which there are sixteen, are all the almond eyed daughters of Confucius and are clothed in the beautiful costumes of the Orient. The girls are all well educated being conversant in Chinese as well as English. Between 7000 and 8000 calls are made each day, and a very peculiar fact about the exchange is that the Chinese call by name instead of number,necessitating the operators being thoroughly familiar with the name and number of every Chinese subscriber. photo shows the main switchboard with some operators at work. 3/16/22

GRAPHIC TALE OF TYPHOON DISASTER THAT STRUCK CHINA.

Just before the Japanese earthquake disaster, a similar catastrophe, but in a much milder form, visited China. A typhoon swept Hongkong and vicinity killing many and doing damage amounting to milkions. Many ships in the harbor were beached and the crews lost. This photo --just received in this country--shows the Steamer Kwong-sai aground at Stonecutter's, near Hongkong.

Un étrange Attelage

Ce n'est qu'en Mongolie que l'on接待re des voitures aussi bizarrement attelées. Et c'est un mode de locomotion qui convient admirablement au pays, vaste plaine où l'on peut galloper pendant des jours et des semaines sans apercevoir une colline.
Il convient non moins aux meurs des habitants, qui sont les?,?,meilleurs cavaliers du monde. On dit d'ieux qu'ils savent monter à cheval avant de savoir marché!
Comme on le voit par notre photographie, les voitures, de forme quasi-antique, sont montées sur des roues très écartées, disposition qui supprime les chances de "versement".
Les brancards sont fixés, d'un bout, à l'axe des roues de devant, et, de l'autre, à une掩 que deux cavaliers reposen sur leurs argons.
De cette façon, ils ne sont pas génés dans leurs mouvements et leurs montures sont dans le même cas. Ils peuvent donc les lancer à Vive allure à travers la plaine.
Il est à peine besoin de faire remarquer que ce bizarre attelage ne peut donner de buns résultats qu'en terrain plot.
Sur une peinte plus ou moins rapide, la voiture aurait ten-dance... à marcher sur les talons des chevaux!
